title: Fact
description:
A mathematical statement as a first-class object, independent of its status.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Every other resource in this repository holds either a formal statement or a status, never both. A `claim` carries prose in `statement` and a CNF *generator recipe* in `formal`, so nothing downstream can reason with what it asserts. A kernel declaration is formal but exists only once proved, and links to no concept, ledger or evidence row. A curriculum node is a topic. A math-education concept is prose with a label. So there was no object that could hold `forall a b : Nat, a + b = b + a` AND say open / conjectured / computed / proved / refuted, with its dependencies and its evidence.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS. A fact is the object the self-extension loop operates on: pick an `open` fact whose `depends_on` are all established, dispatch its `formal.statement` to the solver, reconstruct the result into the kernel, attach evidence, flip the status, record the axiom footprint. Each of those stages exists today and keeps its own incompatible record; this is the shared one.

SELF-CONTAINMENT IS A REQUIREMENT. A fact must stand alone on `formal.statement` plus `status` plus `evidence`. `concept_refs` are provenance and gloss, never substance -- so a public repository works while a source corpus stays private, and nothing needs vendoring or republishing.

RELATION TO `claim`. A claim is an *evidence row about an instance*: it says a specific value was computed and how to re-derive it. A fact is the *proposition*. Claims reference facts through `evidence[].supports`; they are not superseded by them.

id.description: Stable identifier, `F:` prefixed, e.g. `F:nat-add-comm`. Mirrors the `C:`/`TQ:` convention of the concept graph so the two can be cited side by side.

statement.description: The proposition in prose, for a human. Never the machine-readable form -- that is `formal.statement`. Kept because a formal statement alone is not reviewable.

formal.description: What is asserted, machine-readably. This is the field that distinguishes a fact from a claim: a claim's `formal` is a generator recipe, this is the proposition itself.

language.description:
`smtlib2` is dispatchable to the solver; `axeyum-ir` is the internal term form.

`cas-term` is the computer-algebra statement form: a `axeyum_cas::telescoping::HyperTerm` specification (a product of `Γ(linear form)^e`, `base^(linear form)` and `polynomial^e` factors) together with a summation and a claimed closed form, rendered as text. It exists because a definite hypergeometric identity is not expressible in any of the other four: it quantifies over ℕ so it is not `smtlib2`, and no kernel declaration for `Γ`, `∑` or binomial coefficients exists, so writing it as `lean4` would name a theorem the kernel cannot state. The distinction is load-bearing — the whole point of `cas-certificate` facts is that a `cas-term` statement can be settled for ALL `n` by a polynomial identity, and mislabelling the language would make the fact look dispatchable to a machine that cannot read it.

`lean4` means Lean **kernel core**, as emitted by `Kernel::render_lean` — the form `nat_theorem_inventory` prints and the form a fact should normally carry. `lean4-surface` means source syntax intended for the elaborator.

These are NOT interchangeable and the difference is observed, not theoretical: Lean's elaborator inserts pending implicit arguments when a parenthesized application closes, so `(@Eq.refl α) a` fails where the flat `@Eq.refl α a` type-checks. A statement that is valid core can therefore be rejected as surface. One extraction lane had 19 core statements and 1 surface (an iteration the prelude cannot express) and no way to mark the difference except English prose in `notes`.

statement.description: The proposition in the named language. For `smtlib2`, an assertion whose NEGATION being unsat establishes the fact.

fragment.description: The theory that decides it, e.g. `QF_LIA`, `Nat`, `QF_NRA`, or `none` when no fragment we have decides it. Drives reachability queries.

free_symbols.description: Symbols the statement quantifies over or leaves free, so a consumer need not re-parse to know its shape.

epistemic_status.description:
**What THIS system has established.** Deliberately the SAME vocabulary as `claim.schema.json` and the math-education concept graph, plus `refuted`. A fact can be refuted; a claim, being a record of something established, cannot.

This is a statement about our ledger, NOT about mathematics. `open` here means we have not established it, whoever else may have. See `external_status`.

external_status.description:
**What is known to mathematics, independent of us.** Optional; omit when nobody has looked, which is different from `unknown` (nobody has looked *and we checked*).

WHY THIS EXISTS. Without it, `epistemic_status: open` does double duty for two unrelated situations: `Goldbach` (nobody has proved it) and `Fermat's Last Theorem` (proved in 1995; we simply have not imported it). Both are `open` to us and only one is open. That has two concrete costs: the self-extension loop consumes `open` facts, so it would burn its queue retrying settled theorems; and the headline open-count -- a number this project reports -- becomes meaningless.

The first extraction lane hit this immediately and REFUSED to extract Fermat's Last Theorem, correctly, on the grounds that every available status would have been a lie.

THE INTERESTING COMBINATION. `epistemic_status: proved`/`computed` together with `external_status: open`/`conjectured` is not a contradiction -- it is a **new result**, this project's whole point (e.g. R_4(5(x-y)=2z) = 625). The validator surfaces these rather than rejecting them.

depends_on.description: Other facts this one rests on. This is the DAG the build order comes from -- over STATEMENTS, not topics. May be empty for a foundational fact.

proof_route.description:
WHICH machine established this, because `axiom_footprint` is only meaningful — and only comparable — within a route.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Two vocabularies were coexisting in `axiom_footprint` with nothing marking the difference: 17 facts carried `[]` (kernel route, axiom-free) and 14 carried `["axeyum-ir.bool-evaluator", "classical-two-valued-bool-semantics"]` (SMT route, strings a lane had to invent because the field offered none). A reader comparing them would conclude the first group rests on less. That comparison is invalid — they are different trust bases, not different amounts of the same one.

The routes are NOT of equal strength and are not interchangeable. The logic prelude is intuitionistic and carries zero axioms of any trusted kind (measured), so excluded middle, double-negation elimination and Peirce's law are provable on `smt-term-level` and NOT obtainable on `kernel-lean` without a new axiom. A fact settled on one route is not thereby settled on the other, and a reconstruction pipeline that assumes otherwise hits an opaque wall on every classical tautology.

`kernel-lean` — a proof term an independent kernel type-checks. `smt-term-level` — exhaustive evaluation by the IR evaluator, trusting neither bit-blaster, CNF encoder nor SAT solver. `smt-clausal` — decided through CNF, with a DRAT/Alethe certificate. `search-certificate` — a combinatorial search whose result carries a replayable witness or cover. `cas-certificate` — an algebraic identity re-derived by exact polynomial arithmetic that shares no code with the search that found it (Gröbner cofactors `target = Σ cᵢ·gᵢ + r`; creative-telescoping / Wilf–Zeilberger certificates `Σ_j a_j(n)·F(n+j,k)/F(n,k) = R(n,k+1)·r(n,k) − R(n,k)`).

WHY THIS IS NOT `search-certificate`. A witness or cover settles a FINITE statement: replaying it re-derives one instance, and a claim about all `n` needs one certificate per `n`. A CAS certificate is an identity in `ℚ(vars)`, so a single polynomial zero-test settles every instance at once — it is the only route here that can establish a universally quantified arithmetic statement without a kernel proof term. Conflating the two would make `axiom_footprint` incomparable in exactly the way this field exists to prevent, because their footprints differ in kind: a replayed witness assumes only the replay semantics, while an algebraic identity assumes characteristic zero, that the declared term specification denotes the intended summand, and whatever side conditions carry the identity from `ℚ(vars)` to the integers (for telescoping: that `R·F` has the same natural boundary as `F`). Those are real and `[]` is not available here.

axiom_footprint.description:
What the establishing evidence rests on that was NOT itself proved. REQUIRED when `epistemic_status` is `proved`: an empty array means axiom-free and is a strictly stronger claim than an absent field. This is the metric the project publishes.

ONLY COMPARABLE WITHIN A `proof_route`. On `kernel-lean` these are kernel declaration names (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`) and `[]` means the environment admits no `Axiom`, `Opaque` or `Quotient` — a claim `Kernel::axiom_footprint` computes per theorem. On `smt-term-level` they name the semantic assumptions the evaluator makes; `[]` is NOT achievable there and the validator rejects it, because an empty list on that route would read as axiom-freedom the route cannot deliver.

evidence.description: Zero or more artifacts establishing the status. Deliberately the same shape as `claim.schema.json`'s evidence rows so one checker can walk both. A fact with `epistemic_status: open` carries an empty array -- and that is a statement, not an omission.

kind.description: `kernel-term` is a proof term an independent kernel type-checks -- the strongest. `claim-ref` points at an existing `artifacts/claims/` entry, which is how a computed value becomes evidence for a proposition.

checkers.description:
Each INDEPENDENT re-derivation of this evidence, named. `check_status` alone cannot carry this: across the first 50 evidence rows in this ledger every single one said `checked`, so the field had no discriminating power at all, while one lane had in fact validated each result three separate ways — the producing solve, `Evidence::check` against a fresh parse, and an external z3 run — with all three collapsing into that one token.

Cross-oracle agreement is the strongest signal this repository has and it had nowhere to go but prose. List what actually re-derived the result, e.g. ["producing-solve", "Evidence::check-fresh-parse", "z3-4.13"]. Two entries that share an implementation are ONE check wearing two names; the value of the list is independence, not length.

concept_refs.description: Gloss and provenance only, NEVER substance. A fact must be intelligible without resolving these, so that a public repository works while a source corpus stays private.

established_by.description: What settled it: a lane, a solver route, an import, or a person.

source.description: Where the statement came from, if extracted rather than authored.

prior_art.description: Who established this outside axeyum. Required by the validator when `external_status` is settled AND we have not established it ourselves — i.e. when the literature is the only thing holding the fact up.

attribution.description: How the citation itself was obtained — first-class because a lane invented it as a convention and was right to. The honest common case is "standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source", which is a materially weaker claim than having read the paper and must not be silently indistinguishable from it. This project has already cited unrefereed Zenodo self-deposits as though they were published literature.
